chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not entrust me with anything [more] than what he entrusted me with regarding the animosity of the men.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say Jibraeel entrusted him with regarding the animosity of men?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received a unique and paramount revelation from Jibraeel concerning 'mu'adat al-rijal' (animosity toward men), distinguishing it as a primary directive. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific nature of opposition from men as a key component of prophetic guidance, often interpreted as a call to discernment in social and spiritual dealings. The hadith underscores the importance of understanding this animosity not merely as conflict, but as a spiritual test and a defining characteristic of the believer's journey.
